name: Primary Genito-Urinary Tuberculosis

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in endemic tuberculosis regions such as South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, and parts of Eastern Europe

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Composite Clinical, Microbiological, and Radiological Criteria for Genitourinary Tuberculosis

criteria.description: Isolation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex from urine or genitourinary tissue samples
Characteristic radiological findings on intravenous urography, ultrasound, or CT scan showing cavitary lesions, strictures, or calcifications in genitourinary tract
Presence of caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells in biopsy specimens from genitourinary tissue
Chronic sterile pyuria and persistent urinary symptoms unresponsive to conventional antibiotics

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Microbiological confirmation or combination of characteristic imaging findings with clinical features and histopathological evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of clinical, microbiological, radiological, and histopathological data due to paucibacillary nature of disease.

pathognomonic.notes: Persistent presence of white blood cells in urine without bacterial growth
Detected on imaging, characteristic of tuberculosis involvement
searchTerms: cavities or holes in urinary tract
pain in lower abdomen or pelvis

occasional.notes: Indicative of epididymo-orchitis due to tuberculosis
Secondary to tuberculous damage of reproductive organs

occasional.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms (low-grade fever, night sweats, weight loss)
searchTerms: low fever, night sweats, weight loss
general symptoms like fatigue and fever
narrowing of ureters causing kidney swelling
blocked urine flow causing kidney backup

rare.symptomName: Fistula formation between genitourinary tract and adjacent organs
searchTerms: abnormal connections between urinary tract and nearby organs
leakage between urinary and adjacent structures

rare.notes: Due to tuberculous involvement of penile or pelvic structures

rare.symptomName: Renal failure secondary to extensive parenchymal destruction
searchTerms: renal failure due to parenchymal damage
loss of kidney function from extensive damage

laboratory: Sterile pyuria with elevated leukocytes in urine microscopy
Positive acid-fast bacilli (AFB) smear or culture from urine
Positive nucleic acid amplification tests (NAAT) for Mycobacterium tuberculosis
imaging: Intravenous urography showing calyceal deformities, strictures, or cavitations
Ultrasound revealing renal cortical scarring or epididymal masses
CT scan demonstrating genitourinary tract calcifications and hydronephrosis
other: Histopathology showing caseating granulomas with Langhans giant cells
Positive tuberculin skin test or interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA)

distinguishingFeatures: Positive bacterial cultures with common uropathogens
Absence of granulomatous inflammation on biopsy
Eosinophilia and positive serology for Schistosoma species
History of exposure to endemic freshwater bodies

redFlags: Persistent sterile pyuria despite broad-spectrum antibiotics
Development of fistulas or abscesses in genitourinary tract
references: World Health Organization. Tuberculosis fact sheets. 2023.
